content: Man conquers the world by conquering himself.
author: Zeno of Citium
sourceWork: Fragments of the Early Stoa (c. 300 BC)
story:
Shipwrecked off the coast of Attica and losing his entire cargo of Tyrian purple dye, Zeno wandered into a bookseller's shop in Athens, read Xenophon's Memorabilia of Socrates, and asked where such men could be found today. Walking to the Stoa Poikile (Painted Porch), he founded Stoicism, famously declaring: 'Now that I have been shipwrecked, I am on a good voyage.'

In formulating this reflection, Zeno of Citium stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of self mastery. For Zeno of Citium, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?
